title: A Quiet Confession Between Two Coworkers
script: Dinda: [tense] Reza, can I tell you something, and you promise it stays between us?
Reza: Of course. You know I don't repeat things, especially not things that matter to you.
Dinda: [nervously] Last month, a colleague told me something very personal about her family, and she asked me not to share it.
Reza: [reassuringly] Okay. You don't have to tell me the details. What's actually worrying you right now?
Dinda: A few weeks later, another coworker asked me directly if I knew anything about it.
Reza: What did you say?
Dinda: [honestly] For a second, I almost answered honestly, just to seem interesting, or maybe helpful in that moment.
Reza: That's a very human urge, honestly. Gossip can feel tempting for a moment.
Dinda: [firmly] I remembered her trust though, and I simply said, that's not mine to share with anyone.
Reza: Good for you. How did the coworker react to that?
Dinda: [uneasy] She seemed a little disappointed, and she even pushed a bit further, asking more questions.
Reza: Did you stay firm?
Dinda: [determined] Yes. I stayed quiet, even though part of me felt awkward saying no twice to the same person.
Reza: Some trust is more valuable than a moment of interesting gossip. You made the right call, Dinda.
Dinda: Later, my colleague thanked me for something unrelated, without even knowing what had happened at the office that day.
Reza: Does she know how close her secret came to slipping out?
Dinda: [carefully] No, and I don't think she needs to know. That would only make her anxious for no reason.
Reza: That's true trustworthiness, I think. Protecting someone quietly, without even needing them to know you protected them.
Dinda: [reflective] I used to think honesty only meant telling the truth. Now I think it also means knowing when to stay quiet.
Reza: That's a wise way to see it. I’m glad you protected her trust and shared no private details with me.
